chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban from Ibn al-Mundhir who said:
Loneliness was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: Shall I not inform you of something that if you say it, you will not feel lonely at night or during the day?

In the name of Allah and by Allah, and I relied upon Allah, and indeed whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him. Allah accomplishes His command. Allah has decreed a measure for everything. O Allah, make me under Your wing and in Your shelter, and make me in Your security and in Your protection.
So he said: It reached us that a man recited it for thirty years and left it for one night, so a scorpion stung him.

key_terms.قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ قَدْ: Allah has decreed a measure for everything

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for protection against loneliness and what is its significance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes this specific dhikr as a spiritual shield against *wahshah* (spiritual loneliness or alienation), linking inner tranquility to consistent reliance on Allah’s decree (*qadr*). The narration’s concluding anecdote regarding the scorpion sting serves as a practical validation of the dhikr’s efficacy, illustrating how even a single night of neglect can expose one to physical and spiritual vulnerability, a theme deeply resonant in Shia devotional practices.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban, from Ibn al Munzar who said,

‘The loneliness was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> inform you all with something, when you say it, you will not feel the loneliness at night or by the day? (Say),

‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and I rely upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and it is so that the one who relies upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so He<sup>azwj</sup> would Suffice him. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Accomplish His<sup>azwj</sup> Command. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Made an Ordainment for everything. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Make me to be in Your<sup>azwj</sup> Patronage, and in Your<sup>azwj</sup> Vicinity, and Make me to be in Your<sup>azwj</sup> Security and in Your<sup>azwj</sup> Interdiction’.
So he (the narrator) said, ‘It reached us that a man said it for thirty years and neglected it for one night, so a scorpion stung him’.
en.sarwar: Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from more than one person from Aban from ibn al-Mundhir who has said the following: “Once I mentioned fear before abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and he said, ‘I should tell you something that after saying it you will not be frightened during the day or night, say, “In the name of Allah, with (the help of) Allah, I place my trust before Allah; whoever places his trust before Allah, He is suffices him and Allah completes his affairs.
Allah has assigned a measure for everything. O Lord, place me under Your protection, in Your neighborhood, include me in Your amnesty and under Your protection.’
I (the narrator) heard the case of a man who had practiced this for thirty years. He did not say it one night and a scorpion bit him.’”
